title.narrative: Union of Tanzania Press Clubs 2023 -2025 Core support
Union of Tanzania Press Clubs 2023 -2025 Kärnstöd

description.narrative:
The Union of Tanzania Press Clubs (UTPC) is a non-profit umbrella organization registered in 1997 dedicated to uplift journalists in the country by offering training, capacity building opportunities, and coordinating a network of local level support organizations known as Press Clubs.
Support to UTPC started since 2002 on project basis until 2009 - 2011 when the first large project support was funded and followed by strategy core support 2011 -2013. A higher ambition was set in 2016 to 2020 strategy; Was a second time strategy support by Embassy of Sweden that profiled UTPC to another level. At this time UTPC concentrated on activities that would build recognition, accelerate performance, itegrity and network; Journalists were trained on thematic and professional skills; Local networks with like-minded organizations were built, UTPC staff capacities and systems were strengthened, journalists stories of change were produced and ties between government and UTPC started to gain a momentum despite 2015 -2020 regime challenges.
The third UTPC strategy is from 2023 -2025 after extending the 2016-2020 agreement with Embassy of Sweden for a period of two years. The strategy comes with a vision to consolidate interventions and expand working methods by building from the good work achieved in the previous strategies. Embassy of Sweden will support the third strategy with 'core support' and will be its final one after almost 20 years of partnership.
These are UTPC strategy objectives for 2023 - 2025. Firstly, ensuring that Journalists operate with the highest standards of professionalism. The main activity areas to be undertaken concern capacity strengthening of journalists for their professional development. The capacity element will go together with reportage compliance training, monitoring of ethics by ethics ccommittee in press clubs.
Secondly, UTPC will continue to push the agenda that will eventually guarantee for freedom of media and freedom of speech. During this period UTPC will advocate for creation of enabling environment that enable journalists to speak truth to power and to advocate for reforms in the media legal systems. Core to the success of this strategic objective will be engaging the government and working in partnership with other likeminded organization such as Tanzania Human Right Defenders Coalition, Jamii Forums, Legal and Human Rights Center, Coalition on the Right to Information (CoRI) and many more as they will be determined.
Thirdly, UTPC will continue to ensure that Press Clubs operate efficiently, effectively and independently by strengthening the governance systems and capacities necessary to be self-sustaining and hence being able to foster regional and national development by reporting stories of public interest and holding those in power accountable for the benefit of the nation. UTPC believes that the future of existing press clubs will be determined by the strength of the systems installed. This objective will also put more emphasis on thematic specialization. Currently Tanzanian journalist are generalists, as a result quality and in-depth coverage of issues is compromised. Focus is key to developing in-depth expertise in every discipline. Specialized training for key thematic areas and subject specific reporting will be conducted centrally through UTPC and through partnerships with organizations such as BBC Media Action, Jamii Forums, THRDC, CiC (Children in Crossfire), and IMS (International Media Services). Major focus and attention will be in promoting investigative journalism or accountability journalism.
Fourthly is ensuring that Journalists safety, security and wellbeing is protected and respected. The 2022 marks the 10th anniversary since the endorsement of the United Nations Plan of Action on the Safety of Journalists.

Union of Tanzania Press Clubs (UTPC) är en ideell paraplyorganisation registrerad 1997 som stödjer journalister i landet genom att erbjuda utbildning, kapacitetsutveckling och samordning av ett nätverk av stödorganisationer på lokal nivå som kallas pressklubbar. Stöd till UTPC har pågått sedan 2002 på projektbasis fram till 2009 – 2011, då det första stora projektstödet finansierades och följdes av kärnstöd 2011-2013. En högre ambition sattes i strategin 2016 till 2020 som blev ett andra strategistöd av Sveriges ambassad. UTPCs arbete fokuserade på aktiviteter som skulle höja organisationens profil och kompetens. Journalister utbildades i tematiska och professionella färdigheter, lokala nätverk med likasinnade organisationer byggdes, UTPC-personalens kapacitet och system stärktes, journalisters berättelser om förändringar spreds och banden mellan regeringen och UTPC började förbättras trots utmaningarna inom området under åren 2015-2020.
Den tredje UTPC-strategin från 2023 -2025 kommer med en vision om att konsolidera insatserna och utöka arbetssätten genom att stärka de goda resultat som uppnåtts i de tidigare strategierna. Sveriges ambassad kommer att stödja den tredje strategin med kärnstöd och kommer att vara den sista stödperioden.
Följande är UTPC-strategimål för 2023 – 2025:
För det första att säkerställa att journalister arbetar med högsta standard och professionalism. De huvudsakliga verksamhetsområdena som ska genomföras rör kapacitetsförstärkning av journalister för deras professionella utveckling, såsom utbildning i efterlevnad av reportage, övervakning av etik av etikkommittén i pressklubbar. För det andra kommer UTPC att fortsätta driva en agenda för att garantera mediefrihet och yttrandefrihet. Under denna period kommer UTPC att förespråka att skapa en miljö som gör det möjligt för journalister att använda sin yttrandefrihet och att förespråka reformer i mediernas rättssystem. Kärnan för detta strategiska mål kommer att vara att engagera regeringen och arbeta i partnerskap med andra likasinnade organisationer som Tanzania Human Right Defenders Coalition, Jamii Forums, Legal and Human Rights Center, Coalition on the Right to Information (CoRI), IMS och fler.
Vidare är att se till att journalisters säkerhet, säkerhet och välbefinnande skyddas och respekteras. 2022 markerar 10-årsjubileet sedan godkännandet av FN:s handlingsplan för journalisters säkerhet. Som ett bidrag till FN:s handlingsplan kommer UTPC att genomföra journalisters säkerhets- och säkerhetskapacitetsuppbyggnad, tillhandahålla juridisk stödfond, engagera mediaförespråkare i Tanzania om statusen för en säkerhets- och säkerhetsmekanism för journalister, granska och utveckla en mer effektiv säkerhets- och säkerhetsmekanism. Denna process kommer att ske genom konsultativa möten, vilket förhoppningsvis kommer att resultera i en mer strukturerad och praktisk säkerhetsplattform som kan skalas upp brett i Tanzania i framtiden.
För det femte kommer UTPC att reflektera över sina egna system för att granska dem och uppgradera sina strukturer och personal för att stödja sitt uppdrag. Med lärdom av tidigare strategiska UTPC-planer är detta strategiska mål helt fokuserat på kapaciteten inom UTPC att effektivt leverera på planerade insatser. Som en medlemsorganisation som är ekonomiskt kopplad till pressklubbarna är det angeläget att säkerställa att system för ansvarsskyldighet och insyn finns på plats. Byggandet av dessa system kommer till övervägande del att utföras av UTPC och konsulter. Som ett viktigt fokusområde har teamet identifierat behovet av en robust databas och digitala verktyg för att effektivt hantera nätverket och förbättra utbytet av kommunikation, kunskap och finansieringshantering. UTPC-kapacitetsbedömningen under 2018 identifierade flera problemområden för utveckling av pressklubbar.

Thirdly, UTPC will continue to ensure that Press Clubs operate efficiently, effectively and independently by strengthening the governance systems and capacities necessary to be self-sustaining and hence being able to foster regional and national development by reporting stories of public interest and holding those in power accountable for the benefit of the nation. Major focus and attention will be in promoting investigative journalism or accountability journalism.
Fourthly is ensuring that Journalists safety, security and wellbeing is protected and respected. The 2022 marks the 10th anniversary since the endorsement of the United Nations Plan of Action on the Safety of Journalists. As a contribution to UN plan of action, UTPC will conduct journalists safety and security capacity building, provide legal support fund, engage media advocates in Tanzania on the status of a safety and security mechanism for journalists, review and develop a more efficient safety and security mechanism including the recent established platform between government and UTPC with the support from IMS Tanzania. This process will be done through consultative meetings, which hopefully will result in a more structured and practical safety and security platform that can be scaled up widely in Tanzania in future.
Fifthly, UTPC will reflect on its own systems to review them and upgrade its structures and staff to support its mission. Learning from previous UTPC strategic plans, this strategic objective is focused entirely on the capacity within UTPC to deliver on planned interventions effectively and efficiently. As a member organization which is financially linked to the press clubs, the primary concern is to ensure that accountability and transparency systems are in place. Building these systems will predominantly be undertaken by UTPC and consultants. As a key area of focus, the team have identified the need for a robust database and digital tools to effectively manage the network and improve exchange of communications, knowledge, and funding management. UTPC capacity assessment in 2018, had identified several areas of concerns for press club development including ones above.

title.narrative: Union of Tanzania Press Clubs 2023 -2025 Core support
Union of Tanzania Press Clubs 2023 -2025 Core support

description.narrative:
1. Journalists operates with the highest standards of professionalism.
It is reported that JamiiForums and Union of Tanzania Press Clubs (UTPC) collaborated in implementing a comprehensive program aimed at Capacity Building and Mentorship for Journalists in Investigative and Public Interest Journalism (IJ, PIJ), with a focus on digital storytelling. From July 2023, several key activities have been undertaken as part of this initiative. The training, held from the 16th to the 21st of October 2023, brought together 10 journalists (4 females and 6 Males) from different regions across the country (Kigoma, Songwe, Mtwara, Zanzibar, Dar es Salaam, Tanga, Arusha and Iringa regions). The primary goal of the training was to enhance journalists' knowledge and skills in investigative journalism, fostering a commitment to promoting accountability within Tanzanian society.
The 2023 reprot also points out that UTPC implemented what they call the Multi-content and Mobile Journalism Training Program which embarked on a transformative journey across the regions of Mwanza, Ruvuma, Mbeya, Zanzibar, and Arusha, with the primary goal of enriching the skills and knowledge of Tanzanian journalists in Multi-Content and Mobile Journalism. According to UTPC, The project had a transformative vision to provide participating journalists with the essential tools and equipment they needed to support their work effectively.
2. Freedom of information and freedom of the media is guaranteed.
Commemoration of World Press Freedom Day at the National level symbolizes freedom of assesmbly and freedom of expression. UTPC coordinated and organized the event with UNESCO. According to UTPC, the event gathered representatives from the government, the United Nations, development partners, journalists, online and offline media, civil society, human rights defenders, and the research and academic community for thematic discussions in pre-events and side meetings. The same event was commemorated at the regional level by press clubs through debates, roley play, dialogues; The sapace enabled journalists to engage among them selves and with regional government autorities on matters related fournalist safety and security.
It is also reported that UTPC commemorated Democracy Day on September 15, 2023, UTPC observed Democracy Day through an online platform, welcoming more than 100 participants from various media houses, including journalists from press clubs. According to UTPC, some of the key issues highlighted were the decline in journalistic standards, political bias, and credibility issues. The meeting produced resolutions to address the challenges faced by the media sector in Tanzania one of them being; It is crucial to restore the integrity and ethical standards of journalism.
- According to UTPC, the result from the conferences under this objective was the government amendment of Media Service Act in 2023 where 9 out of the 21 proposed amendments were approved. Commeting on these conferences, invited political guest sometimes do ruin schedule and purpose of the meeting. UTPC need to rethink on guests that have potential for such events.
3. Press clubs operate effectively, efficiently, and independently.
UTPC 2023 report says that a three-day coordinators training was conducted in Dar es Salaam with the aim of continue installing the capacity strengthening of moving the UTPC and Press Clubs from Good to Great; Training expected results were, to ensure that all press clubs have active social media accounts, to implement all recommendations from previous reports at the press club level and emphasize on coordination skills, documentation, procurement skills, financial management skills, bank reconciliation, and the preparation of fixed asset register.
Further trainings are reported; Bringing together 112 members (M and F) from press clubs who serve as chairpersons, general secretaries, treasurers, and coordinators. The capacity building training for press club. UTPC also reports to continue support to press clubs by providing office rent, a part of the coordinator's salary, and internet access. In 2023, the Embassy of Sweden reduced its support for press clubs to foster a sense of self-reliance and promote the sustainability of press clubs.
Through support to press clubs, UTPC claims to have achieved the follwoing
- A functional social media account have been established, development of functional systems (manuals at press clubs) and press clubs sustainability. During the reporting period, a total of 7,236 stories were published across various press clubs social media accounts, including Blogs, Online TV, Instagram, Twitter, YouTube, and Facebook. The distribution of these stories is as follows: Drive to Accountability Stories: 852 Information Stories: 4096 stories Educational Stories: 1539 stories Entertainment Stories: 749 stories
- It is also reported that the press clubs have managed to collect a total amount of Tsh 299,602,500/= from various stakeholders among that some was provided by development partners to implement different projects at the press clubs as follows:- Shinyanga press club implemented a project called the voice of media in eliminating violence against women and children with funding of Tsh 53,423, 000/= from Women Funds Tanzania (WFT). Despite of using media as a tool of communication, Pemba press club in collaboration with ministry of health under Zanzibar integrated HIV,Hepatitis, TB, Leprosy Programme (ZIHHTLP) managed a door to door campaign to raise awareness to the community about Tuberculosis (TB). The impact of this campaign at least 105 people tested TB positive and were immediately started treatment at their nearby health center. More than 79 journalists, including 46 men and 33 women, have received awards and appreciation from various stakeholders.
- The press clubs have launched sustainability projects in 2023. For instance, the Simiyu Press Club has implemented a motorcycle project, currently yielding TZS 210,000 per month with its 3 motorcycles. Additionally, they are planning to start a beekeeping project to reduce their dependence. Songwe Press Club planted 1 acre of avocado and half an acre of coffee. For the year 2023 have managed to collect tsh 1,935,000/= Geita press club has a motorcycle project All 28 press clubs managed to prepare their work plan and budget for the year 2023 as well as preparation of their operational manual. It is reported that in 2023 press clubs managed to raise their capital through saccoss/vicoba amounting tsh 102,460,000/= as initiatives to support members on income generation; These initiatives are from the following press clubs Mbeya with the capital of tsh 64,200,000/=, Kigoma capital of Tsh 7,260,000/=, Dodoma 8,500,000/=, Iringa 6,500,000/= and Njombe capital of tsh 16,000,000/=. Based on those figures, it is reported that there is 71% increase of capital from 42,240,000 in 2022.
4. Establish and coordinate Safety and Security mechanisms.
It is reported that, UTPC is coordinating the establishment and management of safety and security mechanisms. The mechanism is established with the aim of supporting journalists on legal and medical.As part of project partnership, UTPC was actively engaged in various activities. One significant initiative involves organizing two National Safety and Security Dialogue for journalists, bringing together journalists and the police force. The 1st dialogue took place on the 19th September 2023 aimed at improving the relationship between the journalists and law enforcers, to promote freedom of expression and access to information, to identify priority areas and practical measures for improving safety and security conditions for journalists, to assess, review and analyze the incidents of press freedom violations reported in 2023.
It is reported that, 24 regional dialogues were conducted in the regions for example Dar es Salaam, Songwe, Manyara, Katavi and Iringa and most of these dialogues were officiated by Regional Police Commanders addressing issues of Safety of Journalists. Issues for discussion were around Press Freedom violations their impact on Freedom of Expression and Access to Information. Safety mechanisms for journalists in Tanzania, and Gender-based incidents in newsrooms and their impact on Media Freedom.
- As a result, The establishment of regional local safety committee have significant improved and strengthened police and journalsits engegment on issue related to safety of journalists. In 2023, six press clubs that conducted safety dialogues were able to establish safety committees at the region level, these are Iringa, Dar es Salaam, Katavi, Mara, Manyara and Songwe. It is assessed that such efforts mark a significant step towards fostering a harmonious relationship between the police and journalists.
5. UTPC cross cutting issues,
It is reported that recognizing the prevalence of gender-based violence in Tanzania, particularly affecting women and girls due to social and economic inequalities, UTPC launched its first-ever campaign against gender-based violence. This campaign agreed with the global 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, running from November 25 to December 10, 2023. According to UTPC, the campaign aimed to amplify the voices of women and girls through journalism, utilizing social media platforms and collaborating with national and international media outlets. UTPC engaged stakeholders through daily discussions and educational content, aligning with the theme "Invest to Prevent Gender-Based Violence."
As a result, Over 1,056 comments were received from participants, with active engagement from both women and men across various regions of Tanzania via WhatsApp groups. Participation of various media outlets, including 68 websites, 9 newspapers, 10 radio stations, and 6 TV stations, actively participated in providing accurate information about gender-based violence throughout the campaign period. This effort was further supported by the dissemination of information through our media outlets, including coverage by international platforms like Voice of America.
To conclude, audit report has 3 pages of the financial statements highlighting achievements made by UTPC by the end of December 2023. In Page 19, there is budget Vs Actual report which shows that UPTC implemented its planned activities at a budget burning rate of 87%. Further review indicates that there are underspends for a number of budget lines some of which are explained by auditors as a result of management reducing cost for unnecessary expenses. Assessment of comparison between audit report and annual narraive report suggests a good correlation and thus indicating that budget was implemented as planned. In terms of results, UTPC has tried to show outcome achieved by each activities performed and that indicates level of improved awareness on impact management conept. Overral, performance and results achieved are assessed as good however more efforts need to be done to press club development or capacity building with a cautious plan, well thought as press clubs are spread across the whole country. A clear strategy is needed and reasonable level of expectaion is required because not all press clubs will grow same pace and at the same time.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
